scope: Complete training-forward GPU work including input conversion, 1D offsets, recurrence/full log_alpha, zero_infinity, loss reduction/output conversion. No backward, host length-stat/dispatch checks, allocator latency or log_softmax preparation.
configuration_search: Same eight configurations for all three variants: BLOCK_S=next_power_of_2(2U+1) times1or2; num_warps1/2/4/8. Confirm union of independently selected per-variant winners across three seeds;9shuffled graph rounds,16repetitions, capture order also shuffled.
source: Pinned FlagGems generic training-forward implementation, revision3f1f896fd90f5db42d167d64fcb9691326071bc2. Distinct no-grad/backward paths are not claims of this study.

correctness.reference: Independent PyTorch CPU FP64 CTC for raw loss, final reduction and every valid log_alpha state/time; full scratch/output bitwise comparison between variants; poisoned outputs and allocation guards; input snapshots.
correctness.tolerance: FP32 recurrence/raw loss atol0.004,rtol3e-5; final BF16 rtol0.01; finalFP32 rtol3e-5. Inf/zero outcomes checked.
correctness.edges: T=1 zero-trip recurrence, empty targets, input lengths0/1/2, repeated labels, 1D/2D targets, FP32/BF16 log_probs, int32/int64 targets. T=0 not executed because unchanged upstream t0 store is out of bounds for zero-sized log_alpha.

barriers: Three source ttg.barrier sites unchanged by AST undo audit; per-specialization final PTX bar.sync count identical across baseline/manual in all139records.
native_contract_result: Every baseline/native-immutable PTX SHA256 pair is identical. Current native pass rejects loops containing ttg.barrier. Manual variant is an upper bound, not evidence that the current compiler performs this optimization.
main_findings: Most gains are modest after independent tuning; several large wins in slow configurations disappear against a tuned baseline.

Held-outT1024,N64,U128,BF16,2D: baseline928.106us versusmanual909.072us best-to-best(1.0209x); pairedseed full ratios1.0208/1.0209/1.0226 andkernel ratios1.0225/1.0231/1.0213. Native no-opcontrol0.99964–1.00025x. Registers38→36;barriers10→10.
TrainingT256,N256,U64,BF16,1D: pairedseed complete-forward speedups1.0645/1.0524/1.0406; kernel-only1.0807/1.0774/1.0590. Registers32→32;barriers9→9.
Short cases have nontrivial graph/control variation; zero-trip workloads have no actual invariant load to eliminate, so apparent small timing differences there are not optimization claims.
decision: A narrow barrier-aware immutable-global-load extension has a small but repeatable performance target. It must retain all barriers and masks, and then be tested on unchanged CTC source; manual timing alone is not a compiler result.
needed_proof: Only an explicitly initialized-at-entry, unchanged-through-all-aliases global input pointer permits moving its ordinary invariant load across CTA barriers. Preserve the original load mask plus loop-entry guard; reject volatile loads, unknown/async effects, calls/assertions, mutable or alias-only inputs, and loads after a potentially nonreached prefix. Do not weaken synchronization or its shared/TMEM ordering.
